task:
Transpiling date arithmetic loses its meaning in several dialects. Fix all of these.

Dropped parentheses. Dialects that write date addition as a binary operator lose grouping, so the math changes. DATE_ADD(a, b) - DATE_ADD(a, b) comes out as a + b - a + b. When such a generated date expression is an operand of another operator, it must be wrapped in parentheses. This covers any binary or unary operator and AT TIME ZONE. There are two exceptions: no extra parentheses when it is already directly inside parentheses, and none when it is the left operand of + or -.

DuckDB read and write:
- SELECT DATE_ADD(TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01', INTERVAL 1 DAY) - DATE_ADD(TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01', INTERVAL 1 DAY) must give SELECT CAST('2024-01-01' AS TIMESTAMP) + INTERVAL '1' DAY - (CAST('2024-01-01' AS TIMESTAMP) + INTERVAL '1' DAY)
- SELECT INTERVAL 1 DAY + DATE_ADD(TIMESTAMP '2024-01-30', INTERVAL 1 MONTH) must give SELECT INTERVAL '1' DAY + (CAST('2024-01-30' AS TIMESTAMP) + INTERVAL '1' MONTH)
- SELECT DATE_ADD(TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01', INTERVAL 1 DAY) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' must give SELECT (CAST('2024-01-01' AS TIMESTAMP) + INTERVAL '1' DAY) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'

Postgres has the same fault. Reading from DuckDB, SELECT DATE_ADD(TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 12:00:00', INTERVAL 30 SECOND) - DATE_ADD(TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 12:00:00', INTERVAL 30 SECOND) must write to Postgres as SELECT CAST('2024-01-01 12:00:00' AS TIMESTAMP) + INTERVAL '30 SECOND' - (CAST('2024-01-01 12:00:00' AS TIMESTAMP) + INTERVAL '30 SECOND'). A multiplied interval must also be grouped in Postgres. Reading from MySQL, SELECT DATE_ADD(col, INTERVAL num_days DAY) FROM t must write to Postgres as SELECT col + (INTERVAL '1 DAY' * num_days) FROM t.

MySQL unit names. MySQL accepts SQL_TSI_-prefixed units in TIMESTAMPADD, but the parser keeps the prefix. For each of SECOND, MINUTE, HOUR, DAY, WEEK, MONTH, QUARTER and YEAR, parsing TIMESTAMPADD(SQL_TSI_<unit>, 1, '2024-01-01') in the mysql dialect must give an expression equal to parsing TIMESTAMPADD(<unit>, 1, '2024-01-01'). Unit names are upper-cased when parsed. SELECT TIMESTAMPADD(SQL_TSI_DAY, 1, '2024-01-01') must write to MySQL as SELECT DATE_ADD('2024-01-01', INTERVAL 1 DAY) and to DuckDB as SELECT CAST('2024-01-01' AS TIMESTAMP) + INTERVAL 1 DAY.

The count in TIMESTAMPADD must stay exact. In MySQL, TIMESTAMPADD(SECOND, '1.000001', '2024-01-01') must give DATE_ADD('2024-01-01', INTERVAL '1.000001' SECOND), and the same for '-1.000001' and '0.000249'. WITH t AS (SELECT '1.000001' AS n) SELECT TIMESTAMPADD(SECOND, n, '2024-01-01') FROM t must give WITH t AS (SELECT '1.000001' AS n) SELECT DATE_ADD('2024-01-01', INTERVAL n SECOND) FROM t.

Subtraction of two TIMESTAMPADD calls: SELECT TIMESTAMPADD(DAY, 1, '2024-01-01') - TIMESTAMPADD(DAY, 1, '2024-01-01') must write to MySQL as SELECT DATE_ADD('2024-01-01', INTERVAL 1 DAY) - DATE_ADD('2024-01-01', INTERVAL 1 DAY) and to DuckDB as SELECT CAST('2024-01-01' AS TIMESTAMP) + INTERVAL 1 DAY - (CAST('2024-01-01' AS TIMESTAMP) + INTERVAL 1 DAY).

Everything else must keep working.
